slides.say: A print shop has twenty-seven printers. Of them, sixteen print in color, thirteen print large posters, and three do neither. How many printers both print in color and print large posters?

So this time neither is given, three, and they ask for both. We have the total, both groups, and neither, so it's an exact question. We'll solve it in two different ways, with the squares method, and then by counting each printer once.
at: So this time neither is given

slides.say: Let's start with the math way, the squares method. We draw four boxes. Neither, posters only, both, and color only. All four together are the twenty-seven printers.
The poster bracket covers posters only and both, thirteen. The color bracket covers both and color only, sixteen.
Three printers do neither, so we write three in the first box.
Neither plus the whole poster bracket is three plus thirteen, sixteen. That covers every box except color only.
The four boxes make twenty-seven. So color only is twenty-seven minus sixteen, eleven.
The color bracket is sixteen, and eleven of them are color only. So both is sixteen minus eleven, five.
So five printers do both jobs. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now by counting each printer once. We start again from the givens. Three printers do neither. So twenty-seven minus three, twenty-four printers do at least one job.
Now we add the two groups. Sixteen plus thirteen is twenty-nine. But only twenty-four printers do a job. Twenty-nine minus twenty-four is five.
Those five extra were counted twice, once in color and once in posters. So five printers do both, the same five.

Careful with choice number two, two. Two is twenty-nine minus twenty-seven. That's what we get if we forget the three that do neither. Choice number four is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number four is our answer
